skill.name: ux-information-architecture
skill.description: [UI/UX] Designs Information Architecture (IA) as ASCII diagrams. Systematically organizes screen hierarchies, navigation structures, and content classification. Use when requesting 'IA design', 'information architecture', 'screen hierarchy', or 'sitemap'.
skill.body:
# UX Information Architecture

A skill that designs Information Architecture (IA) as ASCII diagrams.

## When to Use

- Designing overall screen hierarchy for apps/web
- Defining navigation structures
- Content classification and grouping
- Creating sitemaps

## IA Diagram Symbols

### Hierarchy Nodes
```
[Root]              ← Top level (app/site)
 ├─[Section]        ← Section (category)
 │  ├─[Page]        ← Page
 │  │  └─[SubPage]  ← Sub page
 │  └─[Page]
 └─[Section]
```

### Node Types
```
[Page Name]         ← Regular page
[[Core Page]]       ← Core page (emphasis)
(Modal/Overlay)     ← Modal/Overlay
{Dynamic Content}   ← Dynamic content
<External Link>     ← External link
[Page*]             ← Auth required
```

## IA Structure Patterns

### Hierarchical Tree
```
[Application]
 │
 ├─[Dashboard]
 │  ├─[Overview]
 │  └─[Statistics]
 │
 ├─[Projects]
 │  ├─[Project List]
 │  │  └─{Project Item}
 │  └─(New Project Modal)
 │
 └─[Settings]*
    ├─[Profile]
    └─[Security]
```

## IA Design Principles

- 3-click rule: Major content reachable within 3 levels
- Menu items: 7±2 recommended
- Hierarchy depth: 4 levels or less recommended

generated_query: I’m redesigning the navigation for our e‑commerce platform. We have the following main areas: Home, Shop, Deals, Account, Support. Shop should be broken into Categories (Clothing, Electronics, Home), each with subcategories (e.g., Clothing → Men, Women, Kids). Account includes Orders, Wishlist, Profile, and Settings (password, notifications). Support has FAQ, Live Chat (modal), and Returns. Deals is a dynamic page showing rotating offers. Can you create an ASCII sitemap that shows the full hierarchy, marks authentication‑required pages, and indicates optional modals? Also note that the header has a persistent search bar and cart icon (don’t include those as distinct pages, but they appear on every page).

edit_instructions.rationale: Deleting the auth-required symbol definition prevents the skill from marking authentication-required pages as requested.
Deleting the modal/overlay symbol definition prevents the skill from indicating optional modals as required by the query.
